title: Cryptococcus neoformans: mucicarmine-positive encapsulated yeast
vignette: A 35-year-old man who received a kidney transplant one year ago comes to the emergency department with pleuritic chest pain and cough. He is found to have a low-grade fever. Chest x-ray reveals an infiltrate in the lower lobe of the right lung. The patient is started on broad-spectrum antibiotics, including vancomycin, ceftriaxone, and azithromycin. Despite these measures, his condition worsens over the next several days. Bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage is performed. Mucicarmine staining of his bronchoalveolar fluid reveals round yeast cells surrounded by a thick capsule that stains red with mucicarmine (and appears as a clear halo with India ink) on light microscopy. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's condition?

clues.text: received a kidney transplant one year ago
clues.note: Chronic immunosuppression (transplant) predisposes to opportunistic fungal infections such as Cryptococcus.

clues.text: worsens over the next several days
clues.note: Failure to improve on broad-spectrum ANTIBACTERIALS suggests a nonbacterial (fungal) cause.

clues.text: round yeast cells surrounded by a thick capsule that stains red with mucicarmine
clues.note: An encapsulated yeast whose capsule stains RED with MUCICARMINE (and clears with India ink) is Cryptococcus neoformans - the only pathogenic fungus with a polysaccharide capsule.

whatMatters: An immunocompromised (transplant) patient with pneumonia unresponsive to antibacterials, whose lavage shows an encapsulated yeast staining RED with MUCICARMINE (clear halo on India ink), has CRYPTOCOCCUS NEOFORMANS - the only pathogenic fungus with a polysaccharide capsule. Answer E.
strategy: Anchor on the stain: mucicarmine-positive (red) thick capsule + India ink halo + narrow-based budding yeast = Cryptococcus neoformans (also causes meningoencephalitis). Reject the other fungi by their morphology: Aspergillus (septate acute-angle hyphae), Blastomyces (broad-based budding), Candida (pseudohyphae/germ tubes), Coccidioides (spherules with endospores), Histoplasma (small intracellular yeast in macrophages), Rhizopus (broad nonseptate wide-angle hyphae).

eliminations.label: Aspergillus fumigatus - septate acute-angle hyphae
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a mold with septate hyphae branching at acute (45-degree) angles. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it shows hyphae, not an encapsulated mucicarmine-positive yeast. ✅ Correct if: invasive aspergillosis with septate acute-angle hyphae.

eliminations.label: Blastomyces dermatitidis - broad-based budding yeast
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a dimorphic fungus appearing as a round yeast with BROAD-BASED budding and a thick doubly refractile wall. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it lacks the mucicarmine-positive polysaccharide capsule of Cryptococcus. ✅ Correct if: broad-based budding yeast (Great Lakes/Ohio River region).

eliminations.label: Candida albicans - pseudohyphae/germ tubes
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: yeast with pseudohyphae and germ-tube formation; oral/mucocutaneous/esophageal disease. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it rarely causes pneumonia and shows pseudohyphae, not an encapsulated yeast. ✅ Correct if: thrush/esophagitis or candidemia.

eliminations.label: Coccidioides immitis - spherules with endospores
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: appears in tissue as large, thick-walled SPHERULES containing endospores (Southwest US). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: spherules are not encapsulated budding yeast. ✅ Correct if: spherules with endospores after Southwest travel.

eliminations.label: Histoplasma capsulatum - small intracellular yeast
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: small, oval yeast found INSIDE macrophages (Ohio/Mississippi valleys; bird/bat droppings). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: despite its name, it has no true capsule and is intracellular, not a mucicarmine-positive encapsulated yeast. ✅ Correct if: intracellular yeast in macrophages after cave/bird exposure.

eliminations.label: Rhizopus - broad nonseptate wide-angle hyphae
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a mold (mucormycosis) with broad, ribbon-like NONseptate hyphae branching at wide (90-degree) angles; rhino-orbital-cerebral disease in diabetics. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it shows hyphae, not an encapsulated yeast. ✅ Correct if: mucormycosis in a ketoacidotic diabetic.

reasoning: Immunocompromised transplant patient with pneumonia unresponsive to antibacterials
Lavage shows an encapsulated yeast staining RED with mucicarmine (clear halo on India ink)
The only pathogenic fungus with a polysaccharide capsule is Cryptococcus neoformans
mechanism: Cryptococcus neoformans is an encapsulated, narrow-based budding YEAST whose antiphagocytic POLYSACCHARIDE CAPSULE is its major virulence factor. It is acquired by inhalation (bird/pigeon droppings, soil) and characteristically causes disease in IMMUNOCOMPROMISED hosts (transplant recipients on immunosuppression, HIV/AIDS). Although it most classically causes subacute/chronic MENINGOENCEPHALITIS, it can also cause pneumonia (cough, pleuritic chest pain, infiltrates) that fails to respond to antibacterials. Diagnosis relies on visualizing the encapsulated yeast: the capsule appears as a CLEAR, unstained halo with INDIA INK and stains RED with MUCICARMINE (methenamine silver highlights the yeast cell); the cryptococcal capsular antigen test is highly useful. This encapsulation and staining pattern distinguish it from the other fungi, which show hyphae (Aspergillus, Rhizopus), broad-based budding (Blastomyces), pseudohyphae (Candida), spherules (Coccidioides), or small intracellular yeast (Histoplasma). Treatment is amphotericin B + flucytosine, then fluconazole.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Micro > Cryptococcus neoformans: encapsulated yeast, narrow-based budding; India ink halo + mucicarmine RED capsule; meningoencephalitis (and pneumonia) in immunocompromised; capsular antigen; amphotericin B + flucytosine.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Mucicarmine-positive encapsulated yeast in an immunocompromised host = Cryptococcus.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on polysaccharide capsule, mucicarmine/India ink, narrow-based budding, or meningoencephalitis? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Hyphae = Aspergillus/Rhizopus; broad-based budding = Blastomyces; pseudohyphae = Candida; spherules = Coccidioides; intracellular yeast = Histoplasma.

difficulty.label: 🖼️ Imaging / diagram
difficulty.text: On the mucicarmine stain: round yeast cells with a thick, RED-staining capsule (India ink would show a clear halo). Anchor: 'red mucicarmine capsule / India ink halo = Cryptococcus.'

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: Cryptococcus = only pathogenic fungus with a polysaccharide capsule; India ink/mucicarmine; immunocompromised meningoencephalitis.
